summary: Unexpected dual charges during dedicated burst: reserved commit + per-token metering for same timeframe
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports they were charged both their Reserved Dedicated monthly commit and per-token metering for the same burst window on 2025-01-15 UTC. The invoice line items show a Reserved Capacity prorated charge plus an extra per-token usage line that aligns exactly with a 2-hour burst during peak traffic. Customer believes this is double-billing because their SLA/contract (enterprise reserved pool) should absorb the tokens while their pool scaled out into a hosted burst mode.

Impact:
- Immediate invoice discrepancy of ~$5,400 for the billing period Jan 1 - Jan 15.
- Customer-facing finance team has paused payments pending resolution.
- Application remained functional; no correctness or data exposure issues reported.

Environment:
- Customer account: nimbleretail-prod (org id: 99821)
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (monthly commit) with autoscaling to HostedBurst when capacity exhausted
- Region: us-east
- Affected service components: dedicated-allocator, scheduler, metering, billing pipeline

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Run sustained ingest + chat traffic from 2025-01-15T10:00:00Z -> 2025-01-15T12:00:00Z triggering autoscale and burst into hosted nodes.
2) Observe dashboard: dedicated pool reported full, scheduler routed 37% of requests to hosted-burst fallback during window.
3) After invoice processed, see per-token metering line that corresponds to the same token count during that 2-hour window.

Logs & evidence attached by customer:
- Billing invoice PDF (attached as nimble-invoice-20250115.pdf)
- Sampling of request IDs and timestamps (attached sample_request_ids.csv)
- Console screenshot showing pool scale events and fallback counts (attached scale-events.png)

Investigation notes (support):
- Initial triage (Support): Confirmed invoice contains both prorated reserved commit line and a per-token usage line matching the burst timeframe. Ticket escalated to Billing and SRE for metering trace.
- Billing (Finance): Determined the invoice generator aggregated two separate feeds: reserved commit prorata from the reserved-commit service and a separate usage feed from the metering pipeline. Finance applied a temporary hold and advised Support to find root cause.
- SRE/Serving (Jonah): Preliminary hypothesis: requests routed to hosted-burst were still tagged with the original dedicated pool id by the scheduler during fallbacks; metering pipeline uses routing metadata to decide whether to bill against reserve vs on-demand. If fallback requests carry both tags or incorrect tag, they can be double-counted.
- Observed spike in bridging logs at 2025-01-15T10:05Z where fallback worker A retried and emitted two events: one increment for dedicated counter and one for on-demand counter. Suspect duplicate event emission from the router retry path.

Current status:
- SRE reproduced a narrow-case replay in staging showing duplicate metering increments for routed-fallback retries. Repro steps attached in staging-repro.md.
- Billing has issued a provisional credit for the disputed amount and marked invoice as under review. Finance requests a final explanation before reversing or retaining the credit.
- Engineering has a tentative fix in review to dedupe metering events in the router when fallback routing occurs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2821).

Customer request:
- Formal explanation of what happened and assurance credits will be applied back to the account once root cause is fixed.
- Confirmation that future fallback events will not be double-billed.
- Timestamped audit log showing which tokens were billed to reserved vs on-demand for the disputed window.

Next steps:
- Engineering to finalize and roll out event-dedup patch to staging, run targeted canary for 24h, then promote to prod. (Owner: Jonah)
- Billing to confirm credit issuance and hold until final review complete. (Owner: Maria Chen - Billing)
- Provide customer an export of audit tokens and final postmortem within 5 business days.

Attachments: nimble-invoice-20250115.pdf, scale-events.png, sample_request_ids.csv, staging-repro.md
